children.name: Katharina tunicata
children.description: Katharina tunicata (Wood, 1815), commonly known as the black Katy chiton, black leather chiton, black chiton, leather chiton, or Kasuqix in the indigenous Aleut language, is a species of chiton in the family Mopaliidae.

children.name: Placiphorella velata
children.description: Placiphorella velata, commonly known as the veiled chiton or jockey-cap chiton, is a species of chiton found in rocky crevices from Alaska to Baja California.

children.name: Plaxiphora obtecta P.P.Carpenter, 1893
children.description: Plaxiphora obtecta is a large chiton in the family Mopaliidae, endemic to New Zealand, where it is most often found on the West Coast of the North Island.

children.name: Plaxiphora tricolor Thiele, 1909
children.description: Plaxiphora tricolor is a species of chiton in the family Mopaliidae.

children.name: Mopalia ciliata
children.description: Mopalia ciliata is a chiton in the genus Mopalia, commonly known as the hairy chiton. It is a medium-sized marine mollusc up to 5.0 cm (2.0 in) in length. It is oval shaped with 8 separate, moderately elevated, overlapping ridged valves on its dorsal surface.

children.name: Mopalia hindsii
children.description: Mopalia hindsii is a species of medium-sized chiton that grows up to 7 cm long. Most commonly found in intertidal zones, M. hindsii has a white ventral side unlike most intertidal chitons that are orange underneath.

children.name: Mopalia lignosa
children.description: Mopalia lignosa, the woody chiton, is a medium to large-sized species of polyplacophoran mollusc in the family Mopaliidae. This species was first described in 1846 by the conchologist Augustus Addison Gould and can be found on the west coast of the United States, Mexico and Canada.

children.name: Mopalia muscosa
children.description: Mopalia muscosa, the mossy chiton, is a species of chiton, a polyplacophoran, an eight-plated marine mollusk. It is a northeastern Pacific species which occurs from British Columbia, Canada, to Baja California Mexico.

children.name: Mopalia spectabilis I.M.Cowan & G.M.Cowan, 1977
children.description: Mopalia spectabilis, commonly known as the red-flecked mopalia, is a species of chiton.
